Lipidomic and metabolomic evidence of mitochondrial reprogramming after induction of differentiation

Lipidomic and metabolomic evidence of mitochondrial reprogramming after induction of differentiation. (A-E) Each sub-plot shows representative metabolites from specific pathways while the arrows show known directionality of metabolic flux between interconnected pathways. Glycolysis (A), pentose phosphate pathway (B), lipid β-oxidation (C, D), lipid biogenesis (E, F), and TCA cycle (G) show characteristic changes upon induction of differentiation. Bar plots show the level of various metabolites in NPCs at different time points after induction of differentiation as normalised values to the level of these metabolites at T0. The last column in each plot (Dyn/2) shows the level of these metabolites in dynarrestin-treated NPCs after 2 h of differentiation relative to the level of the metabolites after 2 h of differentiation in control cells. Scatter plots show the level of various lipids in NPCs after induction of differentiation with an experimental set-up equivalent to that described for the metabolites. n = 3 biological replicates. (H) Electron photomicrographs (top) show expansion of smooth endoplasmic reticulum (right, pseudo-coloured red) in differentiating NPCs. Scale bars from left to right 1 μm, 0.2 μm, 0.5 μm. Bottom left inset is a summary of metabolic reprogramming of NPCs during differentiation with the metabolic flux from the upper glycolysis pathway being shunted to lipogenesis
